To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the higher tax morale in northern Europe is an important determinant of the higher tax compliance in northern Europe, 2) the higher tax compliance and lower unemployment in northern Europe is a result of higher concealment costs in northern Europe and not a result of stricter employment protection legislation, and 3) the higher tax evasion in southern Europe is a result, at least in part, of stricter employment protection in southern Europe.

the differences in labour market performance across countries are explained by differences in employment protection legislation and the extent to which the public sector relies on third-party reporting.

the higher informal sectors in southern Europe cannot be explained by differences in tax and punishments systems, but instead by differences in employment protection legislation, tax morale, and use of third-party information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the informal economy on the labour market.
the question of how to reduce the size of the informal sector, and we find that a more flexible employment protection legislation is an effective instrument.
the role of the informal sector for labour market performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both the tax and punishment and the labour market institutions are important for the size of the informal economy, and that the two are intertwined.
a combination of these factors explains the difference in the informal sector.
the differences between the northern and the southern European informal sector cannot be explained by the traditional instruments discussed in the literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the informal sector in Europe is not driven by tax evasion and that the differences between northern and southern Europe are driven by differences in employment protection legislation and tax morale.

the informal sector is a major factor in explaining the differences in unemployment between countries in northern and southern Europe, and that the differences are not due to the tax and punishment regime.
the underground activities in Europe are mainly due to the high cost of being fired in the formal sector and that the underground activities are not a consequence of the tax and punishment systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
labour market policies should take into account that the informal sector is not just a tax haven, but also a place of employment.
the informal sector is a key factor in the labour market, which should be included in the analysis when evaluating policy changes.
the labour market impact of the informal sector depends on the institutional environment and the interaction between the formal and informal sector.
